precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 26:16
precepts.why:
“As the sun when it ariseth in the high heaven; so is the beauty of a good wife in the ordering of her house.” The way she sets it up and the way she does things: that is her beauty.

Ephesians 5 says “as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing.” Submitting “as unto the Lord” means listening to your husband as you would to Christ, and assisting him in what he wants. It is the house of the husband, the house of Abiel, not the house of Abiel and his wife. When you understand whose house it is, you understand whose desires set what the house is supposed to be. If he wants a sound home, give him a sound home; if he wants a clean house, give him a clean house. The confusion comes when a sister thinks her aspirations supersede his. We are on the same team, but somebody is the CEO of the team making the decisions for the franchise.

Be honest, sisters: in the ordering of the house, most husbands let you do pretty much what you want. I don’t give a damn about them pots. The drapes, the knives and forks, the couch set: most men are not tripping over that. As long as he comes home to good food and a clean house, however she got there is fine. So stop acting like submission is straight slavery; most of that is exaggeration. If she wants to lift the carpet and vacuum the cushion every morning, that is her ordering, and that is her beauty.

For the brothers whose wives do not want to clean except when company comes over, cleaning for presentation: you have to order your house. Tell her this is not the desire of your home, this is what needs to be done, and demand it. For the brothers with neat freaks, that is a blessing; sometimes you have to calm them down.

This is also what Titus 2 means by “keepers at home”: a good wife in the ordering of her house, not idle, not a busybody in everybody else’s house, taking care of home.

precepts.label: Ephesians 6:1-4
precepts.why:
“Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right. Honour thy father and mother; (which is the first commandment with promise;) That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth.” “And, ye fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.”

These scriptures are put together with “Put on the whole armour of God” for a reason. If you do half of these things, you are not putting on the whole armour of God; you are putting on pieces. It begins at home. Husbands in order, wives in order; if they are not in order, you can't expect the children to be in order.

Children learn how to obey the Lord by the behavior of their parents, and in turn they are putting on the whole armour of God. The father brings them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord, and that is how a family stands against the wiles of the devil.

precepts.label: Ephesians 5:22-23
precepts.why:
“Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord. For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church: and he is the saviour of the body.”

The whole armour of God is not put on in pieces. If we want to strengthen our families: one, the husband in order; the wife in order; and the children will learn how to obey the Lord by your behavior. The husband is the head as Christ is the head, and the wife submits as unto the Lord.

If the husband and wife are not in order, you can't expect the children to be in order. So the order of the house, the husband as head and the wife submitting, is part of the armour that lets the family “stand against the wiles of the devil.”

precepts.label: Ephesians 5:15-16
precepts.why:
“See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise, Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.”

This is another piece of the whole armour. If you are not redeeming the time because the days are evil, you are not going to teach your children to learn how to fear God. Walking circumspectly, not as fools but as wise, is how a parent sets the example the children follow.

The days are evil: the social media zaps our young out, and Esau sets it up so they can be taken for sweat equity. Redeeming the time means using it for the Lord and for teaching the house, so the family can put on the whole armour of God and “stand against the wiles of the devil.”

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 6:7
precepts.why:
“And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children”. Teach them what? The laws of God. “and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.”

It is a routine of the word. It's repetition: sitting in the house, walking by the way, lying down, rising up. Children are not mature enough to make that cognitive decision on their own; the parent has to put the law in them diligently, over and over.

That is how the children put on the whole armour of God. The husband in order, the wife in order, the time redeemed, and the laws taught diligently at every part of the day, so the house can “stand against the wiles of the devil.”

precepts.label: Ephesians 5:19
precepts.why:
“Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord”.

Over and over you sing these songs, you read these words. It's repetition, the same routine of the word Moses commanded when he said to teach the laws diligently in the house, by the way, lying down and rising up. It is there to mold the children's minds concerning the laws of God.

The world molds them with its music and its social media; the psalms, hymns and spiritual songs mold them with the law. That repetition in the house is part of putting on the whole armour of God, so they can “stand against the wiles of the devil.”

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 6:12
precepts.why:
“Then beware lest thou forget the Lord, which brought thee forth out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage.”

That's why you do it: why you teach the laws diligently to the children, talk of them in the house and by the way, and sing the psalms and spiritual songs over and over. The repetition keeps the house from forgetting the Lord who brought us out of the house of bondage.

Now if you forget the Lord, guess what? You're going to be tempted. Forgetting the Lord leaves the armour off, and the wiles of the devil find a way in. Remembering him is how the family puts on the whole armour of God and stands.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 6:16-17
precepts.why:
“Ye shall not tempt the Lord your God, as ye tempted him in Massah. Ye shall diligently keep the commandments of the Lord your God, and his testimonies, and his statutes, which he hath commanded thee.”

Well, how don't you tempt him? Teach them diligently. Husband in order, wife in order, redeeming the time. Diligently keeping the commandments, testimonies and statutes: that's how you do it, by instructing them.

So all these scriptures go together. Do half of them and you have only pieces of the armour. Do them all, in the house, with the children, and the family has put on the whole armour of God, “that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.”

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 1:5
precepts.why:
Paul speaks of those “Whose end is destruction, whose God is their belly, and whose glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things.” When we overindulge excessively, outside the guidelines God gave us, we start to operate outside the realm of God, outside the realm of discipline, and into the realm of Satan. That is why God gave us a law.

“For the holy spirit of discipline will flee deceit, and remove from thoughts that are without understanding.” The Bible says discipline is a holy spirit. There is a cap and a limit. The man who cannot stop eating is worshipping himself, because God says to eat in moderation and to eat what nourishes; do not eat just to eat. Christ said his meat was to do the will of the Father, but people followed him just for the food, because their god was the belly.

Discipline has to be practiced. People wonder why they cannot obtain discipline: it is because they do not have the Holy Spirit. There is a level of the Holy Spirit given to you because you know your nationality, but there are levels to accessing it and gaining power in it. The disciples reached the level where they worked miracles.

Full access to the Holy Spirit comes through disciplining our food intake and our sex outtake. Food and sex are closely related in the body: one is for procreation of life, the other for nourishing that life. Those two are our stumbling blocks, the two things that keep us from progressing and moving forward.

precepts.label: Sirach 33:29
precepts.why:
“Be not excessive toward any; and without discretion do nothing.” Do not be excessive toward anything. You might say, but I am hungry. Then ask yourself why you are eating. Is it for nourishment, the proper nutrients? Or because it looks good, smells good, tastes good, because you like the sound of it? Are outside things programming you, catering to the lust of the flesh through your eyes and your ears? Did you eat just five minutes ago and now you have to get a snack?

Some are excessive even with sex, a nymphomaniac, wanting sex all the time. Sex was created for procreation; outside of that it becomes pleasure. How much pleasure until the body is completely fulfilled? There is never an end to it. The same with weed: what high are you looking for, when you always come down? There is no fulfillment in smoking weed, drinking alcohol, the excess of sex, or overeating.

That is why the scriptures speak of the holy spirit of discipline. The only fulfillment is in disciplining your spirit and keeping God’s commandments. Once you go outside the realm of discipline, you are catering to the realm of Satan, and you open yourself to be a target and to be controlled at any level. That is the mind of those who “mind earthly things” in Philippians 3.

precepts.label: Romans 16:18
precepts.why:
“For they that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly.” This is the same people Paul wept over in Philippians 3, “whose God is their belly”: the wicked of our people. The scribes and Pharisees could not resist the wisdom of Christ or deny his miracles, but they loved the position Rome placed them in, the accolades, the greetings in the marketplace, and what comes with authority: food and sex. They crept into women’s houses as in Susanna; Eli’s sons exploited the women at the temple, because position and status bring money, power and respect.

They serve their own fleshly pleasures and lusts: let me get over on this person, let me defraud him, let me steal, so I can fill my own belly. Biggie said he was only selling crack to feed his family. He did not serve the Lord Jesus Christ; his own stomach became his god.

Your vessel is an indicator of who you serve. By the way you look, carry yourself, your conduct, your speech and your character, we can tell who your master is. People are going to get mad, but if you are grotesquely overweight, outside the realm of a natural diet, then you are your own god. You say you do not celebrate birthdays, the highest satanic celebration of oneself, yet if you cannot control your food intake, your god is your belly, and that is you.

The good thing is you can control it and do something about it, just like you control whether you celebrate birthdays. God looks at things differently than we do, so we have to reframe our mindset into the mind of Christ and the Father.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 36:25
precepts.why:
“Where no hedge is, there the possession is spoiled.” A bishop must be “One that ruleth well his own house”, and a man who will not lead his house has no hedge around it. If you don’t lead your house, you are going to lose control, and your possession, your wife, will be spoiled.

Failure to lead is one of the things husbands do that destroy marriages. Not stepping up, not taking control of your home, being a passive individual while your wife walks all over you. Eventually some other man is going to come along who catches her eye, and she is going to desire and look to him. Coach Dingolane destroyed a house that way, all because a man would not step up and lead his home.

The flock of God’s pasture are men, and leaders are men. If you are not there guiding, not there instructing, not there correcting, the marriage will come to a crashing halt with her standing over you.

That is why Paul asks, “For if a man know not how to rule his own house, how shall he take care of the church of God?” How can you lead other men and tell them this is the way, if your own house is out of order, if your wife doesn’t listen to you and your kids don’t listen to you? You cannot be over men if you are not able to rule your own house. And the qualities of a bishop are for every man: a bishop is an example of what we are all supposed to be.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 3:7
precepts.why:
“Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel.” Failure to dwell with his wife according to knowledge is another of the things husbands do that destroy marriages, and ruling your own house well depends on it.

A wise husband studies his wife: her fears, her emotions, her struggles, her strengths. That is dwelling with her according to knowledge. When you understand your wife, you are able to guide your house. You push her toward greatness, but you also know her limits, and because you know them you set things up in the home so that things can work. If your wife is emotionally not there to deal with certain things, then you set it up another way. In order to lead, you have to know what they deal with, what they are able to do and what they are not able to do. That goes for your kids as well. You do it now without realizing it: you understand strengths and weaknesses, and you prioritize based on that.

Some men never learn their wives and then wonder why the marriage feels distant.

The other things that destroy a house show the same failure to know her: bitterness and harshness, holding things over her after she has repented and humiliating her, when you are supposed to love your wife as your own self; neglect, when a trip to Walmart is an exciting event for her because you haven’t taken her out, while ordering the house and dealing with the kids all the time is difficult; and withholding love and affection, because if she is not getting it from you, where is she going to get it from? A bishop rules his own house well by dwelling with his wife according to knowledge and giving her honour.

precepts.label: Psalms 42:5
precepts.why:
“For God hath not given us the spirit of fear”. When fear or trouble tries to put you down, David shows how to talk to your own soul: “Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted in me? hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him for the help of his countenance.”

David is speaking to himself, to his soul. Put plain: I might be down, but I'm not broken. I might be down, but I'm not out yet. Satan tried to take me out, but I'm still fighting. My hope is in the Lord, and I still have some fight in me.

Some of you are quick to give up. As soon as something happens, you run out: why did they have to put correction? Correction is a good thing. It keeps you on your toes, it makes you better and stronger. What doesn't break you makes you stronger; that is correction, that is the word of God. You can use a brother's correction to build yourself up: in my mind I was going to do what this brother got corrected for, so let me move from it. Moses said some you correct openly, so that others fear. Some of you never were corrected in your life until you came to IUIC, and you are too prideful to take it.

Brothers, never keep a yes-man around you. If you have a man in your circle who cannot say, bro, I don't think you should do this, that man hates you and is waiting for your downfall. You want men who tell you, don't talk evil of leadership; if you have a problem with a brother, go to him. Sisters are the same: the sister who won't tell you what you want to hear is not your enemy, she is the one you want around you, because she has no respect of persons. Men like that help you get the kingdom of heaven.

precepts.label: Psalms 38:8-9
precepts.why:
David was down but not out, and he did not hide it from God: “I am feeble and sore broken: I have roared by reason of the disquietness of my heart.” To roar is to utter or express in a loud tone: to cry, shout, yell. David says, I'm feeble, I'm broken, and I cried out because of the disquietness of my heart.

“Lord, all my desire is before thee; and my groaning is not hid from thee.” He laid it all before the Lord.

Some of you, when you pray, do not pray for yourself, because you think you are perfect. You need to pray for yourself and ask for help to overcome certain things. Some of you are fighting lust; when you fast, pray that Messiah helps you overcome that lust. We all have lust. Our lust might be different things, but we all have it. Some of you are fighting a covetous spirit; pray that Messiah helps you overcome it.

You are not going to walk into the kingdom of heaven thinking you're perfect and your stuff don't stink. Put your desire and your groaning before the Lord, so that when the storm comes, fear does not overtake you.

precepts.label: Revelation 2:26
precepts.why:
You won't walk into the kingdom thinking you are perfect. This is what Christ said: “And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations”.

The word is overcome. Brothers, you must overcome the lust of America, and you must also overcome the personal thing you struggle with. We all struggle with things. Some of you struggle with lust, with porn, with prostitution, with drugs. Some of you are crackheads, weed heads; some of you it's cigarettes, Black and Milds, women. And yes, it is said to shame you. This is not my word; don't get mad at me. Read what Christ says you have to do.

The words “keepeth my works” mean keep my commandments, keep my laws. My works is this book: keep it. If you keep it, that means you have overcome. You must overcome, or else you are not going to make it to the kingdom.

So when you watch all these prophecies happen, don't include yourself if you won't let the lust go. Some of you need to let things go. That is how you keep from the spirit of fear: you prepare your mind in the scriptures and overcome, so that Esau has nothing to hold over you and you don't betray your brother to hide what you were watching.

precepts.label: Sirach 2:5
precepts.why:
“For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.” You are that gold. We are that gold. How do you purify gold? By putting it in the fire. Some of you need to go into the fire. You have stuff on you that has to be purged out, but you want to keep it and still have the kingdom of heaven. If you don't want to be purged, you cannot get the kingdom. Some of you want to be iron, some of you want to be silver; you have to be that gold.

What is the purpose of going through all that and not getting the kingdom? Esau has been putting you through hell all your life, and you end up missing the kingdom because you hold on to things and don't want God to take the unclean out of you.

Some of you hold on to things that happened fifty years ago, twenty years ago, five years ago. That's like a woman in an argument: you're talking about the orange and she says, yeah, but the pineapple happened five years ago. There's no pineapple here; we're talking about the orange. Some sisters got notes, waiting to bring them out. Men should not be emotional like that.

And “acceptable men in the furnace of adversity”: it takes a strong man to take correction. Weak men cannot. When correction comes, the strong man gets up, repents and keeps moving, and you can tell he is still in the fight. When you get correction, that's when you push harder. Don't lay back. Prove to Messiah, not to leadership, that you are still in the fight.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 9:27
precepts.why:
Peter says to “abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul”, and the two biggest fleshly lusts in the world, going back to Genesis, are food and sex: one deals with nourishing and one with procreation. Paul shows how to fight that war: “But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway.” The whole purpose is to bring our body into subjection, in what we take in through our mouth and what we take in through our eyes.

One way to keep your body in subjection: you can control your sexual appetite and your lust by controlling your food intake. The foods you desire, the foods you like, the foods you are tempted with, practice abstaining from them. Take alcohol. The brain stores alcohol with a time and an environment: late at night, social gatherings, partying, celebrating. So brothers that watch porn, try not drinking when everybody around you is drinking. If you can abstain from that, you can abstain from anything else. You are telling your flesh and your reward vectors, even though my brain says drink in this environment, I am going against what my body wants.

Or the candy you love: abstain from it. If you can abstain from the things you love, you gain control and power over the things that have even more control and power over you. You are training your body and your mind and disassociating things from it until you have full control over your vessel.

Then when it comes to sexual temptation, you tell your body, no, I am not associating this feeling with pornography, this feeling with Instagram, this feeling with looking. Disconnect that association, rewire the neurons, and fire them into a different, positive behavior. When you go into that environment, open up a Bible, do something else, and train your brain to associate that feeling with the new habit. There is a way to get complete control over it, so that having preached to others, you yourself are not a castaway.

precepts.why:
Peter warns, “Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”. Job shows how that adversary works. Satan says to God, “Hast not thou made an hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath on every side?” God had a hedge of protection around Job, and Satan wanted it taken down: “put forth thine hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face.”

God answers, “Behold, all that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thine hand.” Notice what Satan was given. He could take Job's possessions and stir up his life, but he could not touch Job himself, meaning he could not control Job's actions. The devil does not make anybody do anything. He sets the stage, creates an environment to nourish his goal, and watches; you pull your own strings.

Keep reading into Job 2. Satan “smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown”, and Job sat down among the ashes. Then his wife said, “Dost thou still retain thine integrity? curse God, and die.” Satan did not take control of her mouth. He could not get to Job, so he put the thought in the wife, the weaker vessel, because women give in to their emotions and their own thought process more than men do. She had a decision to make, and she chose to act on the thought Satan put in her.

That is the lesson for us. There are spirits in an unseen realm communicating through our minds. You cannot stop a thought from coming, but agreeing with it and acting on it is your choice. America is Satan's stage; everyone acts in the play, but you choose which script you follow.

precepts.label: John 13:2
precepts.why:
“And supper being ended, the devil having now put into the heart of Judas Iscariot, Simon’s son, to betray him”. Look at what it says the devil did: he put it into the heart of Judas. He did not reach in and move Judas's hands. He put the thought there, and Judas acted on that thought and betrayed Christ.

This is the same pattern as Job's wife. Satan works through the thought process. He watches, he looks for the one who will receive the thought, and he plants it. Everything after that is the person's own decision. That is why nobody can say, the devil made me do it. You made you do it.

Peter's warning fits right here: the adversary walks about “seeking whom he may devour”. He is searching for a heart that will take the thought and carry it out, the way Judas did.

precepts.label: Matthew 16:22-23
precepts.why:
Christ told his disciples what was coming: he would be betrayed and killed by the Pharisees, the scribes and the Sadducees. Then “Peter took him, and began to rebuke him, saying, Be it far from thee, Lord: this shall not be unto thee.” Peter was saying, I am not going to allow that to happen.

“But he turned, and said unto Peter, Get thee behind me, Satan: thou art an offence unto me: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but those that be of men.” Christ was supposed to die for the sins of the nation, and Satan whispered to Peter to stand in the way. Christ spotted Satan from a distance, and Peter did not even know Satan was there. That is how crafty and cunning Satan is.

Did Peter have good intentions? He did. But even when good is present, evil is always there. So good intentions are not enough; you have to measure and weigh the words you are about to speak and filter them through the word of God, to see whether this is God's intention or your own desires being worked on by the voice of Satan.

If your mind is not in tune with the scriptures, he can whisper something through your thoughts and take control and manipulate you. Being sober and vigilant means checking even your good ideas against the word.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 6:16
precepts.why:
Wisdom “goeth about seeking such as are worthy of her, sheweth herself favourably unto them in the ways, and meeteth them in every thought.” The devil walks about seeking whom he may devour, and wisdom goes about seeking those worthy of her. Wisdom has to meet you in every thought.

When a thought comes to your mind, measure it: what is the outcome of this thought? Say you get into an argument with your husband. The first thought says, say this certain word, and you can trigger him and make him feel the way you feel. Those thoughts are being fed to you: say this, say this. Wisdom filters that thought and makes sure it has godly intentions before it comes out of your mouth.

Paul wrote in 2 Corinthians 13:10 that he used his words “according to the power which the Lord hath given me to edification, and not to destruction.” The power God gave us is for edification. With every thought, ask: am I exhorting this person, or could the way I am saying it destroy them? Even good intentions and exhortation can land the wrong way.

It works the other way too. Someone may say something to you that was positive when they said it, but it hits you as negative because Satan knows what you are going through and used that person's vessel. Then comes the thought: why would they say that to you? Say this back. You choose whether to respond for edification or unto destruction, whether to bring contention or to wink at ignorance. Everything is a choice.

precepts.label: Genesis 4:7
precepts.why:
God told Cain, “If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door.” Demons do not simply possess someone; it is a process, and they need a series of yeses. The spirits can only communicate through your thoughts and set the stage. To take full control, you have to agree with the thought, make a contract or covenant with it, and act on it. If you say, I do not agree with that, that is not according to the scriptures, the demon cannot take control of your eyes, your ears, your mouth or your tongue.

Doing well is keeping the commandments. It is a covenant with God: I am not going to watch that, eat that, touch that, taste that. Doing not well, sin lying at the door, is a covenant with death, a covenant with Satan. Satan has commandments too, and any time you disagree with keeping God's commandment, you agree to keep Satan's.

See how the yeses add up. You agree to go past the blood alcohol limit and you let a spirit take control of your body, then wonder why you slept with that person. A thought says, I do not like that sister, you agree with it and start gossiping, and now it spreads through the whole body. You know that food is not for you, but you agree with the hunger pains, the sight of it and the smell of it, and now a gluttony spirit is on you. Every contract with a thought lets the demon tunnel through the five senses to full possession of your vessel.

The answer is in Galatians 5:16: “Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.” Walk in the spirit by studying, keeping a strong unit, sitting at the doorsteps of the Bishop and the Deacons, and addicting yourself to God's word, and you will not have time to entertain the flesh. Stop feeding your mind hours of shows and music that taint your thinking. Reprogram and rewire yourself to develop godly habits, because “the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh”.

Christ is the example. His disciples prayed him, “Master, eat”, and he said, “I have meat to eat that ye know not of.” He was the master of his own vessel: his sight, smell, taste, hearing and thoughts. Nobody programmed him but the Father. “My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, and to finish his work.” That should be our agenda: to consume the scriptures, to see, taste, hear and believe them. That is our meat and our life.

precepts.why:
“All things are double one against another”. God created good, and he created evil also. He “hath made nothing imperfect”: Satan was not created imperfect. He was created to do exactly what he is doing, walking about like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour.

“One thing establisheth the good or another”. What establishes the good of us and makes us perfect? When we go through temptation, when Satan attacks us and we overcome and are not devoured by him. Satan does devour some; some brothers and sisters get devoured. But those that are not devoured become better and become perfect. That is why Peter says “after that ye have suffered a while, make you perfect”. It is a hard saying, but without Satan, our adversary, we cannot become perfect, because it is his job and his children's job to try us, and as they try us they make us better. Even the real bad things: Job lost all his kids, and that was to make him perfect.

So learn how to fight him and how to see him when he is attacking. See him when he is coming, when he is trying to jump on you and put thoughts in your mind, and say, get out of my mind, Satan. Don't wait until he puts the thought there and you act on it, and afterward you are like Judas, what did I do? That is why the scripture says be vigilant: vigilant means you are watching.

And “who shall be filled with beholding his glory?” Those of us made perfect in trials and tribulation are the ones who will behold the Lord's glory.

precepts.label: Sirach 2:5
precepts.why:
“For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.” That fire, the furnace of adversity, is temptation. Adversity comes from our adversary, and our adversary is that spiritual demon and his children. So the furnace of adversity in Sirach is the work of the adversary the devil in Peter.

Acceptable men are that gold. When an acceptable man goes through that fire, it doesn't destroy him. It makes him better; it purifies him. When Satan attacks and kills and puts in prison, some men it will destroy, and some men it will make perfect in the sight of God. When the ADL and all these governmental organizations attack us, some of you sisters will be up out of here: I ain't messing with them, the government say they a hate group. Some of you brothers will be gone too. But some of you will be purified and become that pure gold.

You have to go through adversity. Your enemy has to attack you; that is how you become better and how you become a better fighter. Then Peter's words come to pass: “after that ye have suffered a while, make you perfect, stablish, strengthen, settle you.” Nobody wants to suffer, but the Lord says if you want the kingdom you have to suffer, and if you are acceptable, after you suffer you will get the kingdom. Suffering makes you perfect, establishes you, strengthens you until you are battle hardened like somebody who has been warring for thirty or forty years, and settles you within your spirit: it is what it is.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 10:1-6
precepts.why:
Jude says “I will therefore put you in remembrance, though ye once knew this, how that the Lord, having saved the people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed them that believed not.” He is going into history. When we left Egypt we went into the wilderness, and the Israelites rebelled and were put to death. Who else spoke of it in the New Testament? Paul, in Corinthians the tenth chapter. Write that down in your Bible.

“Moreover, brethren, I would not that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud”. Right here it tells you who the people in Corinth were. They weren't white people, weren't Europeans, weren't natural Greeks, Caucasians. They were Israelites: our fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, not Abraham, Isaac and Esau. Under the cloud: the chariot that followed us. They “all passed through the sea; And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea”, because Moses taught the law and taught us Christ, the gospel.

“And did all eat the same spiritual meat; And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.” Christ was always present. “But with many of them God was not well pleased: for they were overthrown in the wilderness”: for murmuring, gossiping, sex, fornication.

“Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things, as they also lusted.” These things were our examples, brothers. That is what Jude puts us in remembrance of: God saved a whole people and still destroyed those who believed not. Don't lust after evil things as they did, and earnestly contend for the faith once delivered unto the saints.

precepts.label: John 3:19
precepts.why:
Jude says the angels which kept not their first estate are reserved “in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day.” Has that great day come yet, brothers? No. Those sons of God who went in unto the daughters of men were destroyed in the flood, and those spirits came right back, by way of the three sons, Ham, Shem and Japheth. They are still here today.

John shows what that darkness is: “And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.” Men loving darkness rather than light is sin: you hate God's laws, you hate this truth, you hate the Bible.

There are people like that who were ordained of old to stay like that, the “certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation”. Remember 2 Thessalonians: God gave them up to strong delusion, that they should believe a lie and not repent and come into the light. Some people are bound in that darkness, and there is nothing you can do for them. That is the chains of darkness, reserved unto the judgment of the great day.

precepts.label: Acts 26:17-18
precepts.why:
Christ sent Paul, “Delivering thee from the people, and from the Gentiles, unto whom now I send thee, To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light”. To open our eyes, and turn us from darkness to light: from sin to righteousness.

Then, “and from the power of Satan unto God”: from the power of Satan, the prince of the power of the air, his evil communication, those unclean spirits that went out of the mouth of the dragon, the beast and the false prophet. So “that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me.”

That is the other side of Jude. Some are bound in chains of darkness, loving darkness rather than light, ordained of old to that condemnation. But the ones Paul was sent to are turned from darkness to light and from Satan unto God, sanctified by faith in Christ. That is the faith once delivered unto the saints that we are earnestly contending for, casting down Esau's lies about fallen angels and Nephilim.

precepts.label: 2 Peter 2:1-6
precepts.why:
“But there were false prophets also among the people, even as there shall be false teachers among you, who privily shall bring in damnable heresies, even denying the Lord that bought them”. This is still going into the same ones Jude speaks of, what Esau calls Nephilim, because they are back today: the evil of our people. “And many shall follow their pernicious ways; by reason of whom the way of truth shall be evil spoken of. And through covetousness shall they with feigned words make merchandise of you”.

“For if God spared not the angels that sinned”. This is not literal angels up in heaven sinning against God. They cannot sin against God; they do his will, and when God tells them to do something, they do it. Stop listening to Esau, the pastors, preachers and congressmen talking about demons, Nephilim and fallen angels. That is a lie. This is the offspring of the sons of God. He “delivered them into chains of darkness”, and that is sin, “to be reserved unto judgment”, the same great day Jude talked about. What they did back then they will keep doing today; they are not going to change.

“And spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly; And turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes condemned them with an overthrow, making them an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly”. He destroyed the old world with water and saved Noah and his whole family.

So nobody is confused: Jude is not talking about Uriel having a fight with an angel, uppercutting him, and the angel falling from heaven. That is garbage malarkey. Black folks live by the saying there is nothing new under the sun, and we get that from the Bible; apply the same logic here.

precepts.label: Acts 12:1-3
precepts.why:
“Behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison”. Did the literal devil come and cast people into prison? Did a spiritual demon snatch somebody and throw him in a cell? No. When the Bible says devil, it is interchangeable: it is talking about the father and his children. The same way we can do nothing without our Father and without the Lord in us, these people can do nothing without their father dwelling in them. He uses his children to do what he wants done.

Acts 12 shows who did it: “Now about that time Herod the king stretched forth his hands to vex certain of the church. And he killed James the brother of John with the sword. And because he saw it pleased the Jews, he proceeded further to take Peter also.” Herod was a white man, an Edomite. He killed James and put Peter in prison. So at that time the devil casting into prison was Herod, Satan’s children, Rome.

The seed of the devil came back as Esau, and the sons of God came back as Jacob: “I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed”. Satan means adversary, accuser, opponent: he is the Lord’s adversary and ours, and so is his seed. Devil means deceiver: as he deceived Eve, his children deceive everyone on the earth. That is why we call the so-called white man the devil, because he deceives the whole earth, and Satan, because he is our adversary and God’s.

So know who we are fighting. This is war, and the devil still casts some of us into prison through his children.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:48-51
precepts.why:
“And to the woman were given two wings of a great eagle”. Who is the eagle? The eagle was Rome at the time, and Rome is an extension of this place called America. Moses tells us about that eagle: “The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth”. That's Rome, when they came in and attacked us in Luke 21, the abomination of desolation of Matthew 24:15, when they destroyed us and ran us out of Jerusalem. From the end of the earth: from Europe.

“a nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand”: we did not understand their tongue when they landed here. Columbus found the Taino, a people who shared food, land and knowledge and fed him as an honored guest, and he wrote that they would make fine servants, and with fifty men he could make them do whatever he wanted. They knew what they came for. Within fifty years the Taino nation was virtually extinct. In Africa they sent explorers, missionaries with Bibles and the cross, and traders with gifts first; they ate at the tables of kings while mapping the gold and rubber, got treaties signed in crafty, ambiguous words, and at the Berlin conference of 1884 sat around a table and split up the continent. They came as swift as the eagle flieth. You can never trust that red man, that devil, that dragon.

“A nation of fierce countenance, which shall not regard the person of the old, nor shew favour to the young”: they didn't care about old or young; they put everybody to death and enslaved everybody. “And he shall eat the fruit of thy cattle, and the fruit of thy land, until thou be destroyed”, and leave neither “corn, wine, or oil, or the increase of thy kine”, kine being cattle, “until he have destroyed thee.”

Then the woman is nourished in her place, and that is America, where we've been nourished through their welfare system, their disability system, their politics, their religions, their educational and economic system. “Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things”. Hungry, thirsty, needing clothing, a passport, a visa, a death certificate, anything we need, we have to go to them. “and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.” The red man put a yoke of iron upon our necks, and we are destroyed today as a people. Even the ones speaking up for us say we love America: that is how destroyed we are.

precepts.label: Revelation 12:9
precepts.why:
The woman is nourished “from the face of the serpent.” Jump to verse 9 to see who the serpent is: “And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world: he was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him.”

That old serpent is the serpent from Genesis. He is called the Devil and Satan, and he deceived everybody; he deceived this whole world. He was cast out into the earth with his angels. That is who the face of the serpent is: the devil himself and his kids, the white man, the red man. They are the enemies Deuteronomy 28:48 says we serve, called the serpent in Revelation.

That is why verse 12 says “Woe to the inhabiters of the earth and of the sea! for the devil is come down unto you, having great wrath, because he knoweth that he hath but a short time.” Woe means death and destruction; this earth is given into the hand of the wicked. He is mad right now, and that is why we are going through it.

And verse 15: “the serpent cast out of his mouth water as a flood after the woman”. That flood is his media, his witchcraft, the same script read word for word on every station, the deceiving of the whole world coming out of the dragon's mouth. But “the earth helped the woman”: this Bible helps us understand what happened to us, what is happening now, and what is going to happen.

Matthew shows it: “the devil taketh him up into an exceeding high mountain, and sheweth him all the kingdoms of the world, and the glory of them; And saith unto him, All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me.” What is the stipulation? “if thou wilt fall down and worship me.” Fall down and worship Satan, and he will give you all this power and authority.

That is exactly what we read at the bottom of Revelation 13:2: the dragon, which is Satan in this part, gave this last beast his power, his nuclear power and armaments, his seat, and great authority. The beast of seven heads and ten horns, the European powers with America as the eighth head, took the offer Christ refused.

On Venice Beach you have people who want to be blessed by Satan: women run through by every so-called movie or music producer who walks up and down that beach, still waiting to be discovered; a man about 90 years old playing the guitar, waiting to be seen by Rolling Stone magazine. People are delusional.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 6:9-10

Satan's stipulation is worship, and many of our people will pay it for money. Paul says, “But they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition.”

“For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.”

That is what Satan will have you do: pierce yourself through with many sorrows, because you covet to be rich in this world. If you covet fame and fortune in this world, you must worship Satan. You must; that is the only way. That is what the Bible is saying.

So the power and the seat and great authority that the dragon gave the beast in Revelation 13 is the same thing he offered Christ on the mountain, all the kingdoms of the world and the glory of them, and the price has always been the same: fall down and worship me. And the angel says the same thing again: “See thou do it not: for I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren the prophets, and of them which keep the sayings of this book: worship God.” He will not take worship, because he is not God. He is a fellowservant, one of the brethren.

precepts.label: Tobit 5:12-14
precepts.why:
Here Raphael, before he makes himself known, presents himself to Tobit another way: “I am Azarias, the son of Ananias the great, and of thy brethren.” An angel of God naming himself as one of the brethren, just as the angel told John, “I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren.”

They are not demonic spirits sent here to oppose the people that inhabit this place called the United Snakes of America. That is untrue. That is popular persuasion; that is lies. This comes as the Lord promises to gather his people: “I will save my people from the east country, and from the west country”, and bring them to dwell in the midst of Jerusalem, “and they shall be my people, and I will be their God, in truth and in righteousness.” The twelve tribes scattered over here until the time of restoration have to flee their idols, their stubbornness and their disdain for the law, to be that people.

That is why we teach God’s laws the way we do. We are not going to the left or to the right with any of you. We are not playing games, because we know why we got over here. We know how we got here: through stubbornness. So if we want to be delivered, we have to wake up.

Judges shows how Israel gets down: “when the judge was dead, that they returned, and corrupted themselves more than their fathers, in following other gods to serve them”, and “they ceased not from their own doings, nor from their stubborn way.” When there is no leader in place, when the officer, the captain, the deacon or the bishop isn’t there, they go back to their lonesome. precepts.label: Sirach 37:27-31
precepts.why:
“Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent: for if thou comest too near it, it will bite thee.” We usually use flee for lust, but you cannot flee from something that is in your refrigerator or your freezer. The brain does not distinguish: the same dopamine and reward centers fire for food that pleases the flesh as for sex. Flee from the unhealthy foods, or they bite you and destroy you. That is why so many brothers have health issues, in the hospital every week and unable to make the Sabbath. You need a healthy vessel to do the work.

Sirach goes further: “My son, prove thy soul in thy life, and see what is evil for it, and give not that unto it.” From verse 27 down to 30 it is literally about food, and spiritually it is about proving your spirit. Just as you see which foods make you sick and unhealthy, see what things are evil for you and make you mentally unhealthy, and give not that unto it. Spartacus was a good show, with a whole lot of sex scenes; you may have to say, I can’t watch this.

“For all things are not profitable for all men, neither hath every soul pleasure in every thing.” A fat brother’s diet is different from a slim officer’s. “Be not unsatiable in any dainty thing, nor too greedy upon meats: For excess of meats bringeth sickness, and surfeiting will turn into choler.” Don’t overindulge beyond your limits, and don’t eat excessively.

Food porn works on the brain the same way pornography does, because the brain sees both as nourishment. There is a healthy pleasure and an unhealthy one: healthy food instead of junk, your wife instead of the screen. Peter says, abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul. When you are counting calories and a 240-calorie cookie calls you with 100 left, you feel that war inside. It is the same temptation, a worldly lust we inherited through America.

“By surfeiting have many perished; but he that taketh heed prolongeth his life.” The Lord is putting us on another level of discipline, because we need brothers fit and in the street teaching.

precepts.label: Sirach 38:17-19
precepts.why:
“Give not over thy mind to heaviness.” Every class is preparing you for what is coming: rent, mortgage, food and gas are going sky-high, ten dollars a gallon, and you will not get a raise. Can you change it? Then why worry about it? “Love thine own soul, and comfort thy heart, remove sorrow far from thee: for sorrow hath killed many.” Stress and worry have killed many, and you are no different.

Sirach shows what heaviness does: “Weep bitterly, and make great moan, and use lamentation, as he is worthy, and that a day or two, lest thou be evil spoken of: and then comfort thyself for thy heaviness.” This is speaking of when somebody passes: mourn, and then comfort yourself.

“For of heaviness cometh death, and the heaviness of the heart breaketh strength.” Heaviness, stress, brings death. And the heaviness of the heart breaks strength: stress makes a man weak. When you are stressed, you don’t want to work out, you don’t want to go to work. Some people eat more; you gain weight, you become fat and sloppy, you lay back, and eventually it is death.

So, brothers, do not let stress wear you down so that you don’t want to do the Most High’s work. Some of you have sat here five or six years in regular clothes. You see the prophecies coming to pass, wars all over the place, World War III a matter of time, and you still sit there. What are you waiting for? What is keeping you back is sin. Examine yourself.

When correction comes, push harder; prove to Messiah you are still in the fight. Don’t hold grudges and keep to yourself, because that is when Satan messes with your head. A merry heart makes a cheerful countenance, but by sorrow of the heart the spirit is broken. The Most High is doing his part. It is time we do ours.

“All that pass by clap their hands at thee; they hiss and wag their head at the daughter of Jerusalem.” All the other nations pass by and clap their hands at us. They are happy we are thrown down, happy we are not exalted, happy we are at the bottom.

“Is this the city that men call The perfection of beauty, The joy of the whole earth?” Everybody knows we are the perfection of beauty: our skin, our hair, our lips, our eyes. Flip the coin and look at Esau, wrinkled and dried up with skin cancer, twenty years old looking forty. And we are the joy of the whole earth: even in the lowest state we are in, everything we do, everybody follows.

“All thine enemies have opened their mouth against thee: they hiss and gnash the teeth.” Starting with Edom on down. You go in the Chinese hair store, the nail shop, the gas station, the Arab store, the East Indian store, and they open their mouth against you; they don’t give a damn about you. “They say, We have swallowed her up: certainly this is the day that we looked for; we have found, we have seen it.” We don’t have a community, only neighborhoods, and in our own neighborhoods they own everything and we are the consumers. This is the day they hoped for, to see us break our laws and fall.

But now the Lord is waking his prophets back up to get his people back in order, to turn this place upside down, so we can have rulership on this earth again in righteousness.

precepts.label: 1 Maccabees 8:24-29
precepts.why:
Rome was such “that, whom they would help to a kingdom, those reign; and whom again they would, they displace”: this is where America got the idea of the coup, of destabilizing countries. Judas Maccabeus was catching so much hell from the Greeks that he went to Rome for help, and these are the articles Rome gave him.

“If there come first any war upon the Romans or any of their confederates throughout all their dominion, The people of the Jews shall help them, as the time shall be appointed, with all their heart: Neither shall they give any thing unto them that make war upon them, or aid them with victuals, weapons, money, or ships, as it hath seemed good unto the Romans”. No food, no weapons, no money, no ships to the other side. Today that is called a sanction. That is why they cut Cuba off and forbid all countries to help Cuba; that is why America told the Caribbean, get rid of the Cuban doctors or we cut off your food supply, and the Caribbean said, we need you, but you have to go.

“In the same manner also, if war come first upon the nation of the Jews, the Romans shall help them with all their heart”: America will help you with all their heart, as long as you are theirs. “According to these articles did the Romans make a covenant with the people of the Jews.” It is the same today: America makes articles with countries, and this is where they got it from.

So when you hear about rebel forces, ask where the money and weapons come from: America, Britain, France or Israel, always one of these European powers. The new president of Syria was an al-Qaeda rebel commander with a $10 million bounty on his head, cleaned up and given a haircut. Out of a country of millions, two or three hundred disgruntled people are given money and promises to overthrow the government. Whom they would, they displace.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 9:16-17
precepts.why:
The prayer is that God would “give you all an heart to serve him, and to do his will, with a good courage and a willing mind.” If you want to return, if you want to repent, he will give you a heart to serve him and to keep his law and commandments. And it must be with a willing mind. Paul shows what that means.

“For though I preach the gospel, I have nothing to glory of”: though we preach the gospel, we have nothing to glory of, because all the glory goes back to the Father. “For necessity is laid upon me; yea, woe is unto me, if I preach not the gospel!” Necessity is laid upon each and every one of us to go out there and wake our people up, so they can repent, come out of it, and cast away their iniquities. Woe unto us if we preach not the gospel.

“For if I do this thing willingly, I have a reward.” We have to do this thing willingly. Nobody can force you. If you do it willingly you have a reward: a crown, everlasting life, immortality. “But if against my will, a dispensation of the gospel is committed unto me.” If you do it against your will, he will take his spirit from you, and you will find yourself back outside those doors in the midst of wickedness and evil again.

So we have to serve the Lord with a willing mind, a sincere heart, and loyalty. We have to come out of all the wickedness we learned here in America, from under the hypnosis given to us here, and serve him willingly.

precepts.label: Isaiah 59:1-2
precepts.why:
The prayer asks God to “send you peace, And hear your prayers, and be at one with you, and never forsake you in time of trouble.” You wonder why you have no peace in your life right now, why you are all over the place? Because you are not serving him, not keeping his law and commandments in sincerity. Isaiah shows what keeps us from being one with God.

“Behold, the Lord’s hand is not shortened, that it cannot save.” His hand is not so short that he can’t reach down and help you when you are afflicted or in trouble. “Neither his ear heavy, that it cannot hear.” His ear is not so heavy that he can’t hear your prayers and your cries and come down and get you out of that situation.

“But your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you, that he will not hear.” That is what separates you from your God: your sins, your iniquities. That is the only way he separates himself from you, if you are in the midst of sin.

But if you are doing what you are supposed to do, keeping the law of commandments in the faith of Christ, he is going to come to you, send you peace, and hear your prayers. If you are sincere and honest with him, walking right in his sight, waking up and returning to him, he will never forsake you in time of trouble. He will help you through your hard times.
